extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, journalists and researchers seeking an encyclopedic summary of Eddie Izzard's life and career
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive Wikipedia-style biographical article summarising the life, career, comedic style, activism and honours of the stand-up comedian and actor Eddie Izzard. Contains career chronology, lists of performances/works, awards, and personal background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic style
rubrics_metrics.description: Izzard's comedic style takes the form of what appears to the audience as rambling whimsical monologues. Izzard uses a stream-of-consciousness delivery that jumps between topics; her bent towards the surreal informed projects such as the sitcom Cows and influences include Monty Python.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and evidence: named tours and specials (Live at the Ambassadors, Definite Article, Glorious, Dress to Kill, Circle, Stripped, Force Majeure, Wunderbar). Commentary notes: she developed her voice through improvisation and street performance; quoted as valuing the 'oral tradition' and surrealism. Implicit evaluative points: originality (rambling/whimsical), improvisational skill, coherence despite topic-jumping, and capacity to create surreal material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual performance / linguistic adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to English, Izzard has performed stand-up in Arabic, French, German, Russian and Spanish; she is fluent in French and learned to perform in other languages since 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: performances in French, and later in Arabic, German, Russian and Spanish; articles note 'Grappling German grammar' and that humour can travel. Implicit evaluative use: ability to perform in multiple languages demonstrates adaptability, cross-cultural reach, and a particular professional skill for a stand-up comedian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career achievements and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Notability is demonstrated by major tours/specials, television series and film appearances, awards (e.g., two Primetime Emmys for Dress to Kill, Tony Award nomination), and recurring high-profile roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence from the page: list of stand-up specials and tours, TV series (The Riches, Hannibal, United States of Tara), film appearances (Ocean's Twelve/Thirteen, Valkyrie, etc.), awards and nominations. Implicit scoring guidance: breadth and prestige of credits and awards indicate career success and industry recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal identity in public persona and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Izzard's gender identity—identifying as genderfluid, use of pronouns, and cross-dressing—has been part of her public identity and has intersected with her performances and public commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes include: she knew she was transgender at an early age, public cross-dressing from the early 1990s, statements about dress not being part of a sexual fetish, and later pronoun/name preferences (she/her, using Suzy Eddie Izzard). Implicit evaluative dimension: how a performer integrates personal identity into material or public image, and how that shapes reception and cultural significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charity work and public-engagement feats
rubrics_metrics.description: Izzard's charity endeavours—most notably completing 43 marathons in 51 days (2009), 27 marathons in 27 days (2016), and other multi-marathon challenges—form a notable component of her public profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence: detailed account of marathon routes, fundraising amounts (£1.35M for Sport Relief in 2016; other amounts noted), BBC documentaries, and awards (BBC Sports Personality special award). Implicit evaluative use: such high-profile endurance challenges serve as measures of public commitment, media visibility, and capacity to mobilise fundraising and attention beyond comedy.
